primary_sources.scope: Definition 2.1 and Remark 2.3: trace and transpose-kernel coordinates.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 and Lemma 3.3: canonical trace, kernel of X, bidiagonal presentation. The separate conormal proof uses kernel of transpose X.
Introduction: Teter number counts canonical-module maps needed to cover the canonical trace. Individual image questions are prior work, with a different domain module.

Theorem 8.5(3), attributed there to Schaps: first-order codimension-two deformations lift the Hilbert-Burch matrix. Differentiating maximal minors gives the conormal trace identity as a classical corollary.
Section 5, Theorem 5.4 and proof: explicit arbitrary-field matrix parametrization gives every first-order deformation of a planar monomial ideal.

sharp_nonattainment_family.uniform_statement: For every field and s>=1, max image dimension=37*s^2, trace length=38*s^2, actual extension length=114*s^2.
sharp_nonattainment_family.proof_of_upper_bound: CT7 with q=(y^s,z^s): the trace quotient has length 5*s^2 and each of four generators contributes at most s^2.
sharp_nonattainment_family.proof_of_lower_bound: The displayed integral map has 37-minors -3 and 4, hence rank at least 37 over every field; free base change multiplies length by s^2.
sharp_nonattainment_family.scope: Bounded rectangle ratio already implies O(n^2) fans for every deformation. No supergeneric fan growth follows.

limits: The complete uniform proofs are in docs/conormal_overlap.md; finite checks do not prove all-field or all-scale statements.

The conormal trace identity is a classical determinantal-deformation corollary; canonical trace and the presentation-kernel framework are established prior work. Exact priority of the capacity application and sharp family is unassessed.
The trace is a sum of all deformation images; it need not equal any single image, including a generic one.
No unrestricted G3 improvement, polynomial lower separation, consequential general complexity theorem or completed goal follows.
